speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: They will undergo postings in ground units, Patrols and Operations, Investigations and Intelligence.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: They may spend some time in MHA getting policy experience and the wider Public Service; sharpen their policy understanding; make them think whole-of-Government.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Some of the younger officers may spend some time with me, assisting me directly.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: And if they perform well, prove they can do the job, they will be appointed to Command positions in SPF.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: SPF today is led by Police Commissioner Hoong Wee Teck.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Rose from the ground, highly respected by the rank-and-file, because he is both operationally very good and at the same time, understands his men and women, so they respect him.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Below him, the Deputy Commissioners: Jerry See, Florence Chua, Tan Hung Hooi.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: They and the next echelons, you will get an example of SPF's approach to grooming leaders and I would illustrate by referring to three officers who are a little bit younger.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Lian Ghim Hua, 41, started again as an Investigation Officer; before that, on scholarship to Cornell and then, Stanford, moved up eventually to become Commander, F Division, which is a stressful position because in terms of crime, it is not the highest, but it covers Prime Minister's ward and coincidentally my ward as well.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: He is now Director of Operations and a high performing officer.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Alvin Moh, age 40, again started as an Investigation officer, Commanding Officer (CO) of Neighbourhood Police Centre (NPC), of which Deputy Prime Minister said something, Commander, G Division, spent time at MHA, now Director of Police Intel Department (PID).

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: All three and others, and the Deputy Commissioners, the Commissioner and people below them, exemplify the SPF leadership today.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: As I said, we also voluntarily gave up various other officers to the wider public sector.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: If we go down the ranks, I will mention three officers with whom I worked directly, again more to illustrate how SPF grooms its leadership.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: One of them is 37, two others are 33 each, spent about 18 months working with me closely: Teo Zi-Ming, 37; Sergius, 33; Lee Huan Ting, 33.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: They went through various ground postings – IOs, CO NPCs and so on – came up to MHA and worked with me.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Zi-Ming is now Assistant Commissioner Commander, F Division at 37.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Sergius is now a Deputy Assistant Commissioner, Deputy Commander, J Division.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Huan Ting is now a Deputy Assistant Commissioner, Deputy Commander, A Division.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: I have mentioned the senior leadership because leadership is vital.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: During this Motion, we recognise all of them: the officer on Coast Patrol, off our waters; the officer in the NPC on ground patrol; officers doing their Emergency Response (ER) patrol, Transport command, Traffic Police, Police Operations Command Centre (POCC) command, Investigation Officers, Gurkha Contingent and many others.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Our Volunteer Constabulary, they are our heroes, unsung, doing their work, day in, day out.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: They are all together, integral to the Singapore that we have today.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: And SPF knows that it must take care of every officer appropriately.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: The SPF today is an institution that is confident and forward-looking.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Officers have a strong sense of purpose, integrity and professionalism.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Morale is high, there is high public trust and confidence in SPF.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: This is the remarkable state of affairs, even more remarkable when you look at the situation of police forces in other cities.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: In the US, police officers nationwide have faced years of protests, there have been calls to defund the police.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Gun violence against police officers have also increased.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Against this backdrop, morale of officers is affected.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Many police departments have trouble finding new recruits.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: The difference between Singapore and these places are not the officers.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: We make it a point to choose very good officers but people for people, Singaporeans, I have said, quality wise, it is difficult to say, draw conclusions.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: The US police force in some states, we learn much from them.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: But the difference is the wider criminal justice system, the laws that can have an impact on the police force and the entire approach of society to the police.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: For example, if you have lax gun control laws, you will get more homicides and more police officers killed.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: And if you are a police officer in the US, as one officer described quite graphically, every time you get a call, whether it is a cat on a tree that is stuck or a baby that has been abandoned, or a neighbourhood call, any call, you go there thinking that someone might shoot you, you go prepared for all eventualities.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: I will illustrate my point by referencing a report by an independent panel called the Report of Daniel Morgan Independent Panel which was released in June this year and received substantial coverage, including in the Financial Times.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: It relates to a person by the name of Daniel Morgan who was a private investigator.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: He was murdered in southeast London in 1987.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: In 2013, finally an independent panel was set up to consider what happened and the independent panel found that the family of Daniel Morgan was failed by police corruption.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: For example, the police officer who had searched Morgan's office was a business associate and later, a colleague of the chief suspect.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: In 2011, the London Metropolitan Police acknowledged, and I quote, "police corruption in our original investigation was a significant factor in this failure".

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: London now has more than 100 murders reported every year since 2015.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: A June 2021 survey shows that only 36% of the population in London have confidence in the police, vis-a-vis 48% nationwide in the UK.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: In a survey of police officers in England and Wales, 85% reported that police service morale was low, 90% cited public treatment of the police had the highest negative impact on morale, amongst other factors including pay and workload.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: It is not because the London police officers are, man-for-man, worse.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: So, I would say to Members, have a care when we look at parts which we have avoided and which we now may feel tempted to go back to.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: The London Met is a highly professional outfit and we learn much from them as well.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: But it is the criminal justice system, the pay of police officers, many other factors.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: It is political will to make sure that the criminal justice system works, that the police officers are protected as long as they have not done wrong and that the system allows for proper investigation and  prosecution, while making sure that innocent people can go free.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Therefore, the entire system works properly with the right balance.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Every police force, including ours, will have errant officers and we have to be most strict, the strictest with our own officers.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: That is a way to make sure that morale is up, integrity is up, public trust and confidence is up.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: So, our officers know, any officer caught wanting will be treated more severely than any member of the public.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: When an allegation is made against any officer, the Internal Affairs Office conducts the investigation.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: If wrongdoing is uncovered, SPF, or in appropriate cases, the Public Service Commission will take disciplinary action against the officer.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Where crimes are perceived to have been committed, there will be charging in Court and the Courts often take into account the fact that this is a Police officer who is charged with upholding the laws, and therefore, the punishment is usually stricter.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: If a further review is necessary, there is an Independent Review Panel, comprising persons of standing, who can review the findings of SPF's own internal investigations.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: As a result, we have been able to maintain public trust, keep up morale and a strong sense of mission within our Police force.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Consistently over the years, a large majority of our officers say that the work they do is meaningful and these are anonymised surveys.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: The work they do is meaningful, they feel engaged with SPF, they identify with SPF's mission, vision and core values.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Internally, Employee Engagement Survey results show very high morale over the last few years.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: The third factor that I want to touch on in explaining SPF's success is the strong trust between the community and the Police.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Mr Patrick Tay and Mr Dennis Tan spoke about this.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: We recognised early on the importance of building trust between the community and the Police.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Over the years, many different community initiatives – the Neighbourhood Police Post (NPP) system, the Neighbourhood Police Centre (NPC) and Community Policing System (COPs) system, the Community Watch groups, Citizens on Patrol, to name a few – have contributed to the high level of trust between community and the Police.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: The public trust in the Police sets the tone for the everyday interactions between the Police and the community.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: When a Police officer arrives on a scene, people cooperate with his directions, they accept that the officer has a right to investigate and manage the incident in the interests of the public.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: And members of the public largely trust SPF.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Many help SPF by sharing crime-prevention messages, providing information on crimes.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Yet others have risked their own safety assisting Police during arrests and live incidents and we make it a point to recognise, honour, praise them and give them an award.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: This level of public trust cannot be taken for granted.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: SPF has to continue to maintain a high level of trust with the community.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: As we reflect on SPF’s progress, we want to pay tribute to SPF officers, past and present, for their contributions and sacrifices.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Our SPF officers across the generations – regular officers, civilian staff, National Servicemen, Volunteer Special Constabulary officers, retired officers – they have served Singapore faithfully and with utmost commitment.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Mr Murali Pillai spoke of 125 SPF officers who have given their lives, and definitely, more than the 125 that you see, in the line of duty.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: He has listed their names in the annex to his speech, to be recorded in the Hansard.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Detective Corporal Yuen Yen Pang and VSC officer Andrew Teo Bock Lan, who were attacked and killed by rioting mobs during the 1955 Hock Lee Bus Riots.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Inspector Allan Lim Kim Sai, who died in a shoot-out with a notorious kidnapper in 1965 – Mr Murali Pillai spoke about him – and his son is here.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Sergeant Mohd Saad bin Omar, who died after being shot by a drug suspect in 1979.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Station Inspector Boo Tiang Huat, who died while on anti-housebreaking rounds in 1994.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: And Staff Sergeant Nadzrie who was involved in a traffic accident while on patrol duties in 2017, four years ago, and I went to his wake.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: These officers and others gave up their lives while trying to keep us safe and secure.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: We remember what they have done for SPF and for Singapore.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: We are privileged to have the families of two of our fallen officers with us in the House today.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Mr David Lim, as you have heard, is a retired Police Superintendent, son of the late-Inspector Allan Lim; and his grandfather was also a Police officer.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: We also have Mdm Chew Tuan Jong and Mr Boo Jia Liang, widow and son of the late Station Inspector Boo Tiang Huat.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: As we commemorate SPF’s bicentennial, we want to recognise the important contributions of SPF and accord recognition to its officers.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Members asked for it, so, I will set out how we will recognise them.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: This includes regular Police officers, volunteer Police officers, full-time National Servicemen and Operationally Ready National Servicemen.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: This Medallion will also be given to civilian officers who were in service with SPF in 2020.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: The Singapore Police Bicentennial 2020 Medal and Medallion are a reminder of SPF’s proud history and of the country’s appreciation of their steadfast commitment in safeguarding our everyday lives.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: From the past to the present and, now, to the future.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: The third part of my speech is that as SPF commemorates its bicentennial, we are looking ahead.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: How can the SPF strengthen itself for the future?

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: First, before the Police officer reports for duty, information on his work assignments for the day will be available through his Police smartphone.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: He will be notified of his patrol sector and partner.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Once in the station, he collects his equipment from the automated systems.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: At the touch of a button, he will instantly draw his communication sets, firearms and taser, his other patrol equipment, such as his riot shield, ballistic-resistant vest.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: His body-worn camera comes equipped with live-streaming capabilities for enhanced sense-making during incidents.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: And his Glock 19 Gen 5 pistol provides higher firepower and ammunition capacity.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: The officer and his partner then get to their Next-Gen Fast Response Car (FRC) equipped with RFID technology as well, which enables them to keep track of the equipment within the FRC.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: They perform a visual check, drive off in the FRC for duties.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Each FRC is equipped with improved safety features and cameras with live-streaming capabilities, feeding back to Police Operations Command Centre (POCC).

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: The victim’s body is found burnt and disposed in a car parked in a secluded location.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: POCC will push the case information to the officers in real time.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: And as officers rush to the scene, SPF investigators will make enquiries.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: At POCC, the extensive network of Police Cameras will allow investigators to quickly narrow down a prime suspect, based on movements caught on camera and also help trace his current movements and whereabouts.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: This sounds hypothetical, but I have based it on a real incident that a body was burnt in a remote location and Police did find the culprit based on cameras and other information.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Investigators access a digitised and automated screening platform.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: The system combs through multiple Police databases, provides case information on the culprit, taking maybe 75% less time to do so than before.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Brings all the databases together, information at fingertips.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Crime scene specialists process the murder scene with advanced technology.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: DNA evidence places the culprit at the scene of the murder.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: The officers then locate the suspect and arrest him.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: This is an SPF that will use technology quite extensively to enhance its operational capabilities and streamline its processes.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Surveillance cameras deployed by governments, whether in Singapore or other countries, are sometimes criticised as being an invasion of privacy.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: These claims overlook a couple of basic point that most people want to live in an environment which is safe and secure.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: And, conceptually, having cameras in public spaces is no different from police interviewing eye witnesses to establish what happened.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: The camera is a constant, ever-present eye witness whose memory would not be suspect.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Surveys also show that people feel safer with the prominent placement of Police Cameras in their own neighbourhoods.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: And they have been very effective in helping Police deter, detect and solve crimes.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: For example, in April this year, there was an armed robbery.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: The suspect was an AETOS Auxiliary Police Officer.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: He had drawn his firearm, changed his uniform, left headquarters without authorisation.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: The potential harm he could have caused was great.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: So, we will install more cameras across the island.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: They help our Police officers to deter, detect and solve crimes, as I have said earlier.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: SPF will also continue to prioritise community policing and step up partnerships with individuals, grassroots organisations, businesses and other public agencies in keeping our Singapore safe.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: The various quotes from Minister Mentor Lee will give a sense to Members.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: He was a key architect, if not the key architect, of modern SPF; and a lot of the philosophy, the approach and the legal system of SPF work came from him.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: So, let me quote: “You need integrity, you need a sense of purpose, you have got to have that mark which others recognise to be special.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Without you, without the quiet civil servant who gets the things done, all the young executives who can wine and dine in Shangri-La, they will be down the drain.” As SPF writes its next chapter, I am confident that SPF will continue to uphold its tradition of excellence and stay anchored on its core values: courage, loyalty, integrity, fairness, even as it charts its way through a more complex operating environment.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: In doing so, SPF must continue to hold its officers to the highest standards of integrity and professionalism, in order to maintain the trust of Singaporeans whom it serves.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: I ask all Members to join me in congratulating and thanking SPF for its 200 years of exemplary service in keeping Singapore safe and secure.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
text: It is a meaningful way to honour SPF's contributions and strengthen the sense of pride and identity amongst Police officers on this significant occasion.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
text: It expresses the collective appreciation of the House for all that our Police officers have done.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
text: Before I move on with my planned speech, I would like to just make reference to Ms Sylvia Lim's comments that the CNB and the ICA were not mentioned.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
text: So, nothing in this Motion dilutes our appreciation to CNB and ICA.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
text: In fact, in 2017, the House debated a Motion, which I moved, on strengthening Singapore's fight against drugs.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
text: And I quote from a speech that I gave that, "the CNB and the Singapore Prisons Services are sterling institutions, staffed with dedicated and committed officers.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
text: Their effort in the fight against drugs is courageous.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
text: But the fight is not only theirs to bear.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
text: All Singaporeans have a role to play." So, nothing in this debate should be misinterpreted as being diluted appreciation to CNB and ICA.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
text: In fact, we hold them also in high esteem.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
text: Looking to the future, over the last 200 years, SPF has displayed an unwavering commitment to keep Singapore and Singaporeans safe and secure.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
text: Our SPF officers have served with integrity, professionalism and courage.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
text: We are proud of SPF's reputation as a world-class Police Force, trusted by Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
text: However, even as SPF continues its transformation and capabilities, it is crucial that SPF and its officers continue to be anchored by the core values of courage, loyalty, integrity and fairness.

speaker: Mdm Deputy Speaker
text: I propose that we take a break now and I suspend the Sitting and will take the Chair at 3.53 pm.

speaker: Mdm Deputy Speaker
text: Sitting accordingly suspended  at 3.33 pm until 4.00 pm.
